question.explanation:
Let $f(x)= \sqrt[3]{x}.$ Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound as $x$ increases. Therefore,

\[ \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} f(x)= \infty. \]

example.title: Evaluating the Limit at Infinity of a Cube Root Function

question.explanation:
We substitute $x=-2$ into the expression, and get

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to \left(-2\right)} \sqrt[3]{x^2-2x}&= \sqrt[3]{(-2)^2-2(-2)} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt[3]{8} \\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*}
